tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

match_key.description: For 'inspect' with 'marker': the attribute to match — label (default), value, or role (the element type, e.g. Button, Switch, TabBar — pass the exact name).

[Tooltip.tsx](HHHHQA/src/globalComponents/Tooltip.tsx) is the component — it renders that dropdown (`HHHH Feedback SP`, `HHHH Bug`, `HHHH Design`, `HHHH User Experience`, `HHHH Quick`, `HHHH Component Page`, `Call Notes`, `Admin Help`, `Help`) and is embedded individually inside dozens of other components/webparts (e.g. [TopNavigation.tsx:307](HHHHQA/src/webparts/updateTopNavigation/components/TopNavigation.tsx:307)), each instance passing its own `ComponentId`.

## Why it's SPA-unsafe (root cause, not a guess)
The component was written assuming **every "page" is a fresh browser load**, which was true for the old HHHHQA experience (each SPFx webpart sits on its own `.aspx` page — clicking to another page = full reload = fresh JS execution). Two things break that assumption in a SPA:

1. **Module-level mutable variables instead of React state** — `pageContent`, `PageUrl`, `Href`, `ComponentData`, `IsSameSite` etc. are declared as plain `var`/`let` at the top of the file ([Tooltip.tsx:15-26](HHHHQA/src/globalComponents/Tooltip.tsx:15)), not `useState`. These are singletons shared by *every* instance of `Tooltip` in the whole bundle. In a full-reload world that's harmless — the module re-evaluates from scratch each time. In a SPA, the module stays loaded, so one instance's click can stomp another's data, and old values leak across navigations.
2. **Context loaded once, never refreshed** — `loadSiteUrl()`/`getCurrentUserGroup()` run in `useEffect(() => {...}, [])` ([Tooltip.tsx:56](HHHHQA/src/globalComponents/Tooltip.tsx:56), [:89](HHHHQA/src/globalComponents/Tooltip.tsx:89)) — mount-once. `pageContext()` itself calls `pnp.sp.site.getContextInfo()` ([globalCommon.tsx:78](HHHHQA/src/globalComponents/globalCommon.tsx:78)) against whatever site `pnp` was configured for at app init — also set once, not per-navigation. If the SPA swaps "pages" without a full reload, `IsHHHHUser`, `taskManagementAvailable`, and the `hhhhteams` site check silently go stale.

## So: new approach or targeted fix?
**Targeted fix, not a rewrite.** The menu logic and link-building itself (`feedbackInitial`) is fine — it's a well-understood "assumed full page reloads, got client-side routing instead" bug class. The fix is: turn the module-level vars into instance-scoped `useState`/`useRef`, and make the context-loading effects re-run when the "current page" changes in your SPA (on route/location change, or by re-keying the component per page) instead of once on mount.

content.text:
That answer confirms exactly what the code shows — I traced the actual mechanism, not just the symptom.

## The mechanism (confirmed in code)

The feedback tool doesn't know "what you're currently looking at" from any explicit state — it reads it off the **browser URL** at click time:

1. [Tooltip.tsx:291-293](HHHHQA/src/globalComponents/Tooltip.tsx:291) builds `Href` from `window.location.href` the instant you click the menu.
2. That gets appended as `&Siteurl=<Href>` to the CreateTask.aspx link ([Tooltip.tsx:132](HHHHQA/src/globalComponents/Tooltip.tsx:132) etc.).
3. CreateTask.aspx then re-parses the task/project id back out of that embedded URL: [CreateTaskComponent.tsx:949](HHHHQA/src/webparts/createTask/components/CreateTaskComponent.tsx:949) does `new URLSearchParams(...get("Siteurl")...).get("taskid")`, and the fallback path at [:625](HHHHQA/src/webparts/createTask/components/CreateTaskComponent.tsx:625) matches Master Tasks by `FoundationPageUrl eq PageUrl` — again derived from the current URL.
4. Same pattern in [TaskProfileComponent.tsx:189-190](HHHHQA/src/webparts/taskprofile/components/TaskProfileComponent.tsx:189): `taskId` for the whole page comes from `new URLSearchParams(window.location.search)`.

**This only works if switching between tasks/projects/portfolios in your SPA actually changes `window.location.href`.** If your webpart's internal router swaps the displayed component/task via client-side state and doesn't call `history.pushState`/update the address bar, the URL stays frozen on whatever page loaded first — so `Siteurl`/`taskId` sent to CreateTask.aspx is stale, and it auto-tags the wrong project/portfolio. That matches exactly what you're seeing.

## Answer to your actual question
No new architecture needed. It's one bad assumption, repeated: "current URL = current record." Fix is to stop deriving context from `window.location` and instead pass the actual current `taskId`/project/portfolio explicitly (props/context) from wherever your internal router holds that state, down into `Tooltip` → into the CreateTask link. Much smaller than a rewrite.

To fix it precisely: **which webpart file is the one with the internal routing** (the one where clicking around doesn't change the address bar)? You mentioned it's a single SPFx webpart — is it `taskprofile` (Task-Profile.aspx) or a different one?

Found it — no more guessing. It's [teamManagementPoratlV3/App.tsx](HHHHQA/src/webparts/teamManagementPoratlV3/App.tsx). That webpart is a genuine SPA: it has its own router (`parseRouteFromUrl`/`applyRouteToUrl`, [App.tsx:56-104](HHHHQA/src/webparts/teamManagementPoratlV3/App.tsx:56)) using `history.pushState`/`replaceState` to switch between Dashboard/Licenses/Hardware/Users/Requests/Concerns/Admin and individual assets — all on **one** SharePoint page, never a full reload.

## The actual bug

The feedback menu is mounted **once**, in the app's persistent header, with a **hardcoded** id:

```tsx
// App.tsx:3364, inside <header>, outside renderContent() — never re-renders per view
<Tooltip ComponentId={14779} />
```

That `ComponentId` is what auto-tags the project/portfolio. Here's the resolution chain in [CreateTaskComponent.tsx:576-604](HHHHQA/src/webparts/createTask/components/CreateTaskComponent.tsx:576):

```ts
AllComponents = await globalCommon.getMasterdataFromIndexedDB();       // "Master Tasks" list, cached
AllComponents = AllComponents.filter(i => i.siteUrl == AllListId?.siteUrl);
...
const compItem = AllComponents.find(item => item.Id == paramComponentId); // paramComponentId = 14779
suggestedProjects = AllProjects?.filter(p => p.Portfolios?.some(port => port.Id == paramComponentId));
```

So the "auto-tag" isn't computed from the page or URL at all — it's a lookup: `ComponentId` → a row in the **Master Tasks** list → that row's parent Project/Portfolio. This worked in the old architecture because **every page had its own row in Master Tasks with its own id**, so a hardcoded id-per-page was correct.

The new portal broke that assumption without anyone changing the feedback code: one SPA page now stands in for what used to be Licenses page, Hardware page, Users page, each individual asset's page, etc. — but it still only ever sends `14779`, for everything. If `14779` isn't a row registered in Master Tasks for this site (very likely — it's a new webpart, no old page to register), the lookup just returns nothing and no project/portfolio gets tagged, regardless of what you were looking at.

## Two different fixes, depending on what you actually want

1. **Feedback should always tag one fixed project/portfolio for this whole portal** (reasonable if "Team Management Portal V3" is itself one project) — this is a **data fix, not code**: register `14779` (or whatever id you pick) as a row in the Master Tasks list for this site, pointed at the right Project/Portfolio. Nothing to change in App.tsx.
2. **Feedback should tag the specific asset/license/user/concern currently open** — this needs a real code change: stop hardcoding `ComponentId={14779}` and instead pass the id of whatever's currently selected (you already track `familyId`/`userId`/selected asset in the route state), then either register each of those in Master Tasks too, or extend `CreateTaskComponent.tsx` to resolve project/portfolio from something other than the Master Tasks id lookup for this app.

Which of these matches what you want feedback to do here?

content.text:
## Problem (Hinglish mein)

Jo purana HHHHQA tha, usme **har feature ka apna alag SharePoint page (.aspx) hota tha** — Licenses ka alag page, Hardware ka alag page, har asset ka apna page. Aur har page pe feedback burger-menu ke andar ek **fixed `ComponentId` hardcode** kiya hua tha (jaise `1626`, `7801`, `14779` etc.), jo "Master Tasks" list ke ek row se match karta tha, aur wo row batata tha ki "ye page kis Project/Portfolio ka hai." Kyunki 1 page = 1 cheez, isliye 1 fixed ComponentId kaam kar jaata tha.

Ab naya **Team Management Portal V3** ek real SPA hai — pura Dashboard, Licenses, Hardware, Users, Requests, Concerns, Admin, aur har individual asset **ek hi page** pe, andar-andar client-side routing se switch hote hain (URL bhi change hota hai but full reload nahi hota). Lekin feedback menu (`<Tooltip ComponentId={14779} />`) **sirf header mein ek baar mount** hua hai, aur `14779` **hamesha same fixed value** bhejta hai — chahe aap Dashboard pe ho, kisi specific Asset pe ho, ya kisi User ke profile pe ho.

Isliye jab CreateTask.aspx us `14779` ko Master Tasks list mein dhoondta hai to project/portfolio galat (ya khaali) resolve hota hai — kyunki wahi ek id sab views ke liye use ho rahi hai, current asset/user/license ka pata hi nahi chal raha.

## Plan (Option 2 — per-record tagging)

1. `App.tsx` mein already route state hai (`view`, `familyId`, `userId`, `assetTitle` — [App.tsx:33-40](HHHHQA/src/webparts/teamManagementPoratlV3/App.tsx:33)). Isi se pata chal sakta hai user abhi kaunsa specific record dekh raha hai.

Bilkul sahi samjhe — ComponentId → Master Tasks lookup wala mechanism **already correct hai**, poore codebase mein yehi pattern har jagah use hota hai. Asli problem sirf itni hai ki Team Management Portal V3 ek hi SPA hai jisme **9 alag-alag "screens"** hain, lekin sirf **1 hi ComponentId (14779)** poore app ke liye fixed hai. Fix simple hai: **har screen ko apna khud ka distinct ComponentId do**, jaise baaki poore codebase mein hota hai (1 id = 1 screen/feature).

`App.tsx` ke `renderContent()` mein maine ye 9 distinct "screens" dekhe:

1. Dashboard (`case 'dashboard'`)
2. Licenses (`case 'licenses'`)
3. Hardware (`case 'hardware'`)
4. Users list (`case 'users'`)
5. Requests (`case 'requests'`)
6. Concerns (`case 'concerns'`)
7. Admin (`case 'admin'`)
8. Asset/Family Detail (`selectedFamilyId` branch → `AssetProfile`)
9. User Profile Detail (`selectedUser` branch → `UserProfile`)

Plan: `<Tooltip ComponentId={14779} />` ko global header se **hata denge**, aur har screen ke render ke andar apna khud ka `<Tooltip ComponentId={...} />` daalenge — bilkul waise jaise `inlineEditingcolumns.tsx` mein `7801` ya `SubPointBottleneckAction.tsx` mein `15436` fixed hai per-screen.

**Ek cheez jo mujhe SharePoint access na hone ki wajah se khud nahi ho sakti**: ye naye ComponentIds real numbers honge — unhe pehle "Master Tasks" list mein **Component-type row banakar register karna padega** (Title + sahi Project/Portfolio se link), tabhi unko actual `Id` milegi jo main code mein hardcode karunga. Ye exactly wahi kaam hai jo purane pages ke liye already kiya gaya tha unke apne ComponentIds ke liye.

To sequence ye rahega:
1. Aap (ya jinke paas Master Tasks list access hai) 9 naye Component rows banao — ek har screen ke liye, sahi Project/Portfolio se tagged.
2. Mujhe wo 9 naye Ids do.
3. Main `App.tsx` update kar dunga — global `14779` hata ke har screen mein uska sahi id daal dunga, **koi fallback nahi**.

content.text:
Samajh gaya — matlab **ComponentId to already sahi track ho raha hai**, us mein kuch fix nahi chahiye. Wo padhta hoon confirm karne ke liye:

Har jagah `<Tooltip ComponentId="15436" />` jaisa call hota hai, wo ek **React prop hai, JSX mein directly likha hua** — SPA ho ya na ho, ye hamesha us exact call-site se hi aata hai, kabhi mix-up nahi hota. Toh "kis component se feedback tool use hua" — **ye part already sahi hai, isme koi change nahi karna**.

## Asli dikkat: Task URL

Ye check kiya — [Tooltip.tsx:18](HHHHQA/src/globalComponents/Tooltip.tsx:18) mein `Href` ek **module-level shared variable** hai (`var Href = ''`), poore Tooltip.tsx bundle ke liye sirf ek hi. Jab bhi koi Tooltip instance pe click hota hai, [getQueryVariable()](HHHHQA/src/globalComponents/Tooltip.tsx:284) chal ke `Href = window.location.href` set karta hai — matlab **Task URL hamesha "abhi jo browser address bar mein URL hai" wahi hota hai**, chahe feedback kisi bhi nested component/popup se click kiya ho.

Ye theek chalta hai **sirf tab jab us specific component/row ka apna unique identifier URL mein already ho** (jaise `?taskId=123`). Lekin jo components popup/modal ke andar hain (Bottleneck, QuickView, EditTask jaise) — wo apna URL kabhi update nahi karte, chahe SPA ho ya purana system. To unke liye Task URL hamesha sirf "page ka generic URL" bhejta hai, us specific item ka nahi — **ye galti purane system mein bhi thi, SPA ki wajah se nayi nahi aayi, bas ab zyada nazar aa rahi hai.**

## Fix

`Tooltip` component mein ek naya **optional prop `TaskUrl`** add karenge:
- Agar calling component apna sahi, specific URL pass kare (`<Tooltip ComponentId="15436" TaskUrl={myOwnRecordUrl} />`), Tooltip usi ko use karega — `window.location.href` ko ignore karke.
- Jis component ko apna distinct URL pass karna zaroori hai (jahan multiple records/rows ek hi page pe hain), usko khud apna URL banana hoga (jaise us record ka id query-string mein daal ke).

Iska matlab — **no silent fallback**: jis bhi call-site pe `TaskUrl` nahi diya gaya, wahan Task URL sirf current page ka URL jaayega jaisa abhi hai (jo simple/single-record pages ke liye sahi hi hai) — koi galat guess nahi hoga.

Ab batao — kis file/page se shuru karna hai? Aap jo 4 pages bol rahe ho unme se pehla konsa hai, uska path do, main seedha wahi khol ke `Tooltip`/calling-component dono update kar dunga.
